text.p: Following are the highlights of the main stories in the Bosnian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- International agencies in Bosnia, in a letter sent to the Moslem-Croat federation president Vladimir Soljic and his deputy Ejup Ganic, say the events in Jajce over the weekend when hundreds of Moslem returnees to the Jajce area were forced to leave their homes by Croat mobs, were unacceptable.

- NATO-led Stabilization Force (SFOR), Office of High Representative for Bosnia (OHR), UN agencies, International Police Task Force (IPTF), and Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), requests that within 48 hours the conditions are created for a safe return of Moslem families who had to leave their homes in Jajce.

- Mirza Hajric, an aide to the Bosnia's presidency chairman Alija Izetbegovic, says the Moslem side insists that a list of ambassadors be extended with by more countries, which are "Bosnia's proved friends". These are Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Quatar.
- The ruling Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) will adopt a resolution on Gorazde, says Hasan Cengic, the SDA main board member and a deputy in the federation parliament.
- Reconstruction of the Gorazde region in eastern Bosnia will be the SDA's priority in next four years.
- Commission for property requests by refugees and displaced persons in Bosnia solved about 3,400 requests for property return by July 31.
- Tuzla airport can open two months after the memorandum on understanding about civil aviation is signed, says the Tuzla airport director Mustafa Terzic.
- Some 800,000 to 1 million German marks will be needed to open the Tuzla airport.
- If the Council of Ministers members do not reach an agreement on law on citizenship and passports on Monday, the High Representative to Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp, will introduce penalties.

- Women refugees from Srebrenica protested on Sunday over the statement of the Sarajevo cantonal interior minister Ismet Dahic that they hurt policemen in Vogosca suburb on Friday, while the policemen did not hurt them.
- Srebrenica women blocked the visit of Vogosca Serbs to the Orthodox graveyards on Friday afternoon and stoned policemen who tried to protect returnees.
- A Bosnian bus was attacked and robbed by unknown persons on Sunday near the Croat-controlled town of Busovaca.
- Moslem-Croat federation parliament's House of Representatives will not convene until the conditions for its work are created, says its president Mariofil Ljubic.
